analyst_view.overall: Albacete have won three league games in a row under Joseba Etxeberria and press high and fast, but are without José Corpas (suspended), Javi Moreno, Fran Gámez, Higinio and Munir, with San Bartolomé a late doubt after an ankle knock in the cup. Celta Fortuna are missing Quique Ribes, Joel López and Adrià Capdevila (suspended) plus Cuenca, Kibet and Mateo Sobral on international duty, and call up six youth players, though Anxo Rodríguez and Óscar Marcos are back. Monday-night kick-off at the Carlos Belmonte.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and I hold there. Celta Fortuna's games have been open (19-25 in 13) and a squad full of youth players can be exposed, but Albacete have scored only 13 in 13 and lose Corpas and Munir, which keeps the total from climbing.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with 6.3 for Albacete. I lean mildly lower, to about 9.6: Etxeberria's side win the ball high and attack quickly rather than camping in the opponent's half, and Celta Fortuna, who pass more by LaLiga's count, should have more of the ball than the split suggests. It is a style read, so the size is small.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards. I lean higher, to about 5.9: Albacete's pressing invites fouls, Celta Fortuna arrive with three players banned for yellow-card accumulation, and a game between two sides near the bottom should be scrappy. Mild size, since the numbers already expect a busy game.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots; I would take about 25.4. The cut is mainly on Albacete's side: LaLiga counts them at under nine shots a game, so 16.1 at home looks generous, especially without Corpas, Munir and Higinio, three of their attacking options.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target; I would take about 8.6, in line with the lower shots. Óscar Marcos is back for Celta Fortuna, which helps Álvaro Marín, but the rest of their attack is young and Albacete's wins have come from few attempts.
